subject: English Home Language

source.subtopic: Uses words pronounced and spelt the same with different meanings (fly: the verb and the insect)

show.line: A fly is a little insect. To fly is what birds do. Same word, two meanings. The sentence tells which!

rounds.story: A fly landed on my bread. Which picture shows this fly?
The bat flew out of the cave at night. Which bat?

rounds.prompt: Thabo hit the ball with his bat. Which bat?
I can see the ... in the sky, and I can ... a kite. Same word. Say it.

rounds.story: Gogo put the ring on her finger. Which picture shows this ring?

rounds.prompt: Which meaning? Sort the pictures. A thing, or an animal?

rounds.story: Papa will seal the envelope. A seal swims in the sea. Which picture shows the sea animal?

hints: Read the whole sentence. The other words tell you which meaning.
Picture it in your head. Does an insect fit, or a flying bird?

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! The bat hit the ball. I will pick the picture.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: A furry bat with wings hit the ball!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! A bat that hits a ball is a cricket bat. The sentence tells us.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's read it together. Hit the ball. That needs a cricket bat!

parent_line: Can work out which meaning a word has from the sentence.
